profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a publicly traded semiconductor and AI technology company founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California. Its website, focused on the Nemotron product line, describes the company as building multimodal foundation models intended for enterprise agentic AI applications spanning reasoning, vision, speech, retrieval-augmented generation, and safety. NVIDIA reported revenue of approximately $215.9 billion for the fiscal year ending January 25, 2026, according to its most recent 10-K filing.

The company's Nemotron family is described on its site as a collection of highly efficient, multimodal, open AI models built for long-running, self-evolving agents, with support for platforms including NVIDIA RTX PRO and NVIDIA DGX Spark. Specific models mentioned include Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, aimed at faster task completion, and NeMo Switchyard, which routes tasks to appropriate models. Nemotron models are available both as openly licensed releases, under the NVIDIA Open Model License, which permits use, modification, distribution, and commercial deployment without attribution, and as NVIDIA NIM microservices requiring an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license for secure, scalable deployment. Bryan Catanzaro, described as VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, is cited on the site discussing the rationale behind open model development. Additional tools mentioned for running Nemotron at scale include NVIDIA Dynamo, TensorRT-LLM, and NIM, alongside open-source libraries SGLang and vLLM.

The held facts note that NVIDIA carries 187 tracked legal exposure items associated with California, though no specific cases are listed. The company trades on a public exchange under the ticker NVDA with CIK 0001045810 on file with the SEC.
